anomalies.observed: The main VDD pins of both MCUs are isolated single-pin nets. NAVC1 VSS pins are tied only to each other rather than to GND, and NAVC1 VSSA is unconnected. The +3V3 net used for MCU-side pull-ups/connectors has no regulator source and no MCU VDD nodes.
anomalies.expected: The specification states that the 3V3 rail feeds both MCUs. Standard MCU practice requires all VDD pins connected to the 3.3V supply and all VSS/VSSA pins connected to ground.

evidence.quote: 3V3 feeds both MCUs (FCC, NAVC) and all I2C sensor ICs

anomalies.impact: Both MCUs are effectively unpowered and/or lack a ground return, so the board cannot boot or perform its intended flight-control/navigation function.

anomalies.observed: FCC1 VCAP power pins are connected directly to the UART3 connector nets: pin 48 (VCAP) is on UART3_TX_FCC and pin 73 (VCAP) is on UART3_RX_FCC.
anomalies.expected: STM32H7 VCAP pins are internal-regulator decoupling/power pins and should be connected to VSS/VDD with the required capacitors, not to UART signal nets.
anomalies.impact: The MCU internal regulator decoupling pins are shorted to UART lines; this can prevent MCU startup, corrupt UART3, and likely damage or latch up the MCU.

anomalies.observed: The FCC HSE crystal is connected to FCC1 PE6/PE7, while FCC1 PH0/PH1 are only loaded to caps and PH1 is used as the VREF+ filter net. The NAVC HSE crystal nets do not connect to NAVC1 PH0/PH1 at all.
anomalies.expected: The specified high-speed external crystal for both MCUs should connect to the MCU HSE pins PH0/PH1, with VREF+ and VDDA connected to their dedicated analog pins.
anomalies.impact: The external 25 MHz clock is not applied to the intended HSE pins, and analog reference connections are also misassigned; the MCU may fail to start, run on an unintended internal clock, or have invalid analog/reference behavior.
